/-!
# Erdős Problem 1068

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1068](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1068)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Cardinal SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos1068

/--
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain a countable subgraph which is
infinitely connected?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1068 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_  1 →
      ∃ s : Set V, s.Countable ∧ InfinitelyConnected (G.induce s) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1068

reformulations.difference: Lean requests an induced subgraph on a Countable vertex set, rather than an arbitrary countable subgraph. Bowler–Pitz explicitly describe the requested subgraph as countably infinite.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adding edges on the same vertex set preserves infinitely many distinct, pairwise internally vertex-disjoint simple paths. Thus any qualifying subgraph H yields the qualifying induced graph G.induce H.verts; conversely an induced graph is a subgraph. Furthermore, InfinitelyConnected excludes every finite graph: it requires two distinct vertices and infinitely many distinct simple paths between them, whereas a finite graph has only finitely many simple paths. Hence Countable introduces no finite witnesses. The full quantified equivalence with existence of a countably infinite arbitrary subgraph was proved as Review1068.problem_iff_countably_infinite_subgraph in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
